articles.title: How to layer without the bulk
articles.excerpt: Three thin layers beat two thick ones. Here is the order we build in, and the one piece that quietly does most of the work.
body: Start with the finest layer you own and work outward in weight. A merino crew under a poplin shirt under a wool coat will always look sharper than a chunky knit under a padded jacket, because each layer keeps its own shape.
Keep the shoulders consistent. If the outer layer has a dropped shoulder, the piece beneath it must too, or the sleeve will bunch at the armhole and add visual weight you never asked for.
Leave one thing unfinished. An unbuttoned cuff, an open collar, a hem left loose. Precision everywhere reads as effort; one loose end reads as confidence.

articles.title: The case for one good coat
articles.excerpt: Double-faced wool has no lining, no glue and no shortcuts. We explain why that changes how a coat falls — and how long it lasts.
body: A double-faced fabric is woven twice and joined in the middle, so there is no separate lining and no fusible interlining holding the front panel in shape. The result is a coat that drapes from the shoulder instead of standing away from the body.

Because the seams are sewn and then closed by hand, the join lies flat and never bubbles after dry cleaning. It is slower and more expensive to make, which is exactly why so few coats are made this way.
Look after it simply: brush after wear, rest it a day between wears, and dry clean no more than twice a season. A good coat should outlive the trend that brought you to it.

articles.title: Dressing for a day with two plans
articles.excerpt: Desk, then dinner, then whatever comes after. The three-piece formula we use when the day refuses to stay in one lane.
body: Choose one base that works hard — a fluid trouser or a straight jean — then build two tops around it. The first should be quiet enough for a morning, the second strong enough for a night.
Outerwear is your pivot. A long coat over a plain tee is a completely different sentence to the same tee under a cropped, sharp-shoulder jacket. Change only that and you have changed the whole look.
Shoes and one accessory carry the rest. Keep them deliberate, and let the clothes stay easy.
